page: Microsoft Azure F16alds_v7 is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor capable of reaching 4.5 GHz clock speeds. It operates with a single thread per core, eliminating hyper-threading contention. Memory allocation is configured at 32 GB total, establishing a 2 GB per core ratio. Cache structure features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The CPU exposes modern vector and cryptographic instruction extensions, notably AVX-512 with BF16 and VNNI extensions, AES, and SHA-NI. The instance bundles 1,888 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and operates without discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results validate the high clock speed of the underlying AMD processor, placing the instance in the top tier for single-core execution across both Geekbench and stress-ng tests. Data transformation tasks demonstrate exceptional throughput, with single-threaded gzip compression achieving 41.2 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression reaching top-tier ratings. Image and text processing also achieve top-tier marks in Geekbench tests. In AI inference evaluations, small language model text generation achieves top-tier throughput at over 400 tokens per second. Multi-core compute benchmarks, including Geekbench multi-core and PassMark CPU evaluations, maintain solid upper-quartile to mid-tier performance, while uncached memory bandwidth reads of 116.72 GB/sec support steady data throughput.

The configuration emphasizes compute density over memory volume, delivering strong compute efficiency for workloads constrained by raw clock speed and vector execution rather than massive memory footprints. The integration of 1,888 GB of fast local NVMe SSD provides significant scratch space without incurring external storage latency. However, the 32 GB memory ceiling makes the instance less suited for large in-memory databases or large-scale analytical datasets. The F16alds_v7 is optimal for CPU-bound compilation pipelines, continuous integration runners, image and text processing pipelines, lightweight machine learning inference, and high-frequency batch processing workflows.
description: Microsoft Azure F16alds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine equipped with 16 dedicated physical x86_64 cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz. Configured with a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, it includes 32 GB of system memory (2 GB per vCPU) alongside 1,888 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, while omitting dedicated GPUs. The AMD architecture incorporates advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support. In performance benchmarks, the instance demonstrates top-tier single-core performance across stress-ng and Geekbench, excelling in compression, decompression, and lightweight LLM inference token generation, alongside strong multi-core throughput. Memory bandwidth and static web serving tests reflect balanced, standard-tier results. Due to its lean memory profile paired with high-frequency dedicated compute and fast local disk, this server offers efficient resource utilization for CPU-intensive compilation, image and text batch processing, and caching compute pipelines that do not require high memory density.

32 GB system RAM configured at a compute-optimized 2 GB per vCPU ratio
